                                                                                  handshake
handshake

Handshake synchronization. Default Severity: evaluation.
Crossing: data bus; Promotion: cdc_handshake (default: on) FX: yes (default on).

Specifying the cdc scheme on directive with the -handshake option directs CDC static analysis to
identify DMUX synchronization schemes as handshake CDC schemes. Like DMUX synchronization,
handshake synchronization uses a synchronized select signal to enable a data MUX to pass through data
to the receive clock domain. Handshake synchronization has additional synchronization of the receive
data MUX select signal, which is fed back to the transmit clock domain select logic. This "round-trip"
synchronizer circuit automatically resets the receive domain MUX select signal. The enable signal to the
transmit data MUX select also activates the receive data MUX select via the round-trip synchronizer.

Examples

     1. The following is an example to turn severity to caution:

            cdc scheme on handshake
            cdc report scheme handshake -severity caution

2. In the following CDC report entry, the two synchronizers are the two 2DFF synchronizers in the
     round-trip synchronizer circuit.

      Cautions
      =================================================================
      Handshake synchronization. (handshake)
      -----------------------------------------------------------------
      ClkO : start : DMUXInLtch (Sync_ReqAck.v: 107)

            ClkR : end : DMUXOutLtch (Sync_ReqAck.v: 114)(ID:handshake_21466)
            Synchronizer ID : two_dff_17913
            Synchronizer ID : two_dff_28075
        Request Signal: ReqInO
        Acknowledge Signal: AckIn

3. The following example shows an instance of a handshake scheme. This scheme is a special case
     of a DMUX scheme and by default, is reported as such. To turn on HANDSHAKE reporting:

Questa® CDC User Guide                                                            527
Reference

handshake                                                                       

     cdc scheme on handshake

     The following code implements handshake synchronization:

     // transmit data register

     always @ (posedge tx_clk)

           if (enable & ack_synced) tx_data <= din;

     // receive data register

     always @ (posedge rx_clk)

           if (ack) rx_data <= tx_data;

     // generate request

     always @ (posedge tx_clk) req <= (req | enable) & !ack_synced;

     // generate acknowledge

     always @ (posedge rx_clk) ack <= req_synced;

     // acknowledge synchronizer in TX domain

     always @ (posedge tx_clk) begin: ACK_SYNC

           reg  temp;

           temp <= ack;

           ack_synced <= temp;

     end

     // request synchronizer in RX domain

     always @ (posedge rx_clk) begin: REQ_SYNC

           reg  temp;

           temp <= req;

           req_synced <= temp;

     end

     Handshake synchronization. (handshake)
     -----------------------------------------------------------------
     tx_clk : start : tx_data (handshake.v : 11)

                 rx_clk : end : rx_data (handshake.v : 11) (ID:handshake_7492)
                 Synchronizer ID : two_dff_24576
                 Synchronizer ID : two_dff_36232
                 Request Signal: req
                 Acknowledge Signal: ack

hdm_sync

A user-specified HDM or custom synchronizer module might contain synchronization logic connected to

multi_bits

Multiple-bit signal across clock domain boundary. Default Severity: violation.
Crossing: multibit data bus; Promotion: cdc_sample (default off); FX: yes (default on).

An unsynchronized CDC data bus in most cases should be a static violation. Similarly, a CDC data
bus synchronized using a 2DFF synchronizer should not drive any logic from the wire connecting the
two flip-flops. However, some data buses from test or configuration logic might be constant or ad hoc

multi_clock_memory                                                                                   

multi_clock_memory

Memory with different read and write clocks where read and write are independent. Default Severity:
caution.
Crossing: data bus; Promotion: none; FX: no.

By default, CDC analysis reports memories with different read and write clocks as FIFO memories and
FIFO-style memories (see FIFO Memory and FIFO Crossings). FIFO-style crossings that pass the criteria
for FIFO memories are identified as fifo_memory crossings.

You can use cdc scheme on fifo to enable FIFO detection. If the FIFO read and write pointers (addresses)
belonging to the read and write domains are correctly identified, CDC analysis searches for the pointer
synchronizers. If the synchronizers are detected, a FIFO evaluation is issued. However, address
synchronizers may not be found if the memory is not intended to be a FIFO. So, CDC analysis also
looks for improper address crossings to other clock domains. If unsynchronized address crossings
are not found, the tool assumes that the memory is not intended to be a FIFO, and categorizes it as a
multi_clock_memory. In this case, the write and read domains may be writing to and reading from the
memory independently. The default severity of this scheme is caution. You must verify if the intent is to
read from and write to the memory independently with different clocks.

The detection of multi_clock_memory requires CDC analysis to search for improper address crossings,
which can increase the runtime. So, multi_clock_memory detection is disabled by default. To enable it,
use cdc scheme on multi_clock_memory.

Examples

     1. To enable multi-clock memory detection:

            cdc scheme on fifo
            cdc scheme on multi_clock_memory

     2. To enable FIFO detection and report the multi_clock_memory scheme:

           netlist port domain wr_addr -clock wr_clk
           netlist port domain rd_addr -clock rd_clk
           cdc scheme on multi_clock_memory
           cdc scheme on fifo
           module dut(

               input wr_clk, rd_clk ,
               input [7:0] wr_data,
               input [2:0] wr_addr, rd_addr,
               output reg [7:0] rd_data);

               // The mmory array is a FIFO.

532                                                                         Questa® CDC User Guide
                                                            Reference
                                               multi_clock_memory
               reg [2:0] Mem [7:0];
               always @(posedge wr_clk) begin

                   Mem[wr_addr] <= wr_data;
               end

   always @(posedge rd_clk) begin
       rd_data <= Mem[rd_addr];

   end
endmodule

multi_sync_mux_select

MUX select fan-in contains more than one synchronizer. Default Severity: caution.
Crossing: control signal or data bus; Promotion: cdc_dsel (default on), cdc_hamming_one (if enabled
with cdc signal -mutually_exclusive); FX: yes (default on).

Crossing type is reported for multiple-synchronized signals in the fanin of an enable.
Use the cdc preference dmux directive to recognize CDC crossings as DMUX schemes where Tx or Rx
signals are memories (but not black box memories).

Examples

     1. The following is an example to turn severity to evaluation:
            cdc report scheme multi_sync_mux_select -severity evaluation

     2. The following is an example to turn off promotion:
            cdc promote scheme multi_sync_mux_select -promotion off

     3. A DMUX synchronizer with multiple control signals synchronized in the Rx domain:

534                    Questa® CDC User Guide
                        Reference

                        multi_sync_mux_select

  module dut (
     input clk1,
     input rx_clk,
     input sel1,
     input sel2,
     input data,
     input data2,
     output reg rx_data

  );

  reg tx_data;
  reg mux_out;

   /* TX */
  always @(posedge clk1) tx_data <= data;

  reg tx_sel1, s1_sel1, s2_sel1;
  reg tx_sel2, s1_sel2, s2_sel2;
  always @(posedge clk1) tx_sel1 <= sel1;
  always @(posedge clk1) tx_sel2 <= sel2;

   /* Synchronizrs */
  always @ (posedge rx_clk) begin

   s1_sel1 <= tx_sel1;
   s2_sel1 <= s1_sel1;

   s1_sel2 <= tx_sel2;
   s2_sel2 <= s1_sel2;
  end
   /* MUX */
  always @* begin
   if(s2_sel1 & s2_sel2)

     mux_out = tx_data;
   else

     mux_out = rx_data;
  end

   /* RX */
  always @(posedge rx_clk) rx_data <= mux_out;

  endmodule

mux_lock_dmux                                                                                               

mux_lock_dmux

MUX lock enable. Default Severity: caution.
Crossing: synchronized control signal and muxed data bus; Promotion: cdc_dsel (default off); FX: yes
(default on).

The mux-lock DMUX scheme is a restricted version of the general DMUX scheme. For the general
scheme, the fanin logic of the Rx signal can contain any logic and the synchronized control signal can
use any logic to turn off the Tx signal (not just a MUX). The control signal can be synchronized by any of
the following signal synchronizers: two_dff_phase, dff_sync_gated_clk, four_latch, two_dff, pulse_sync,
dff_sync_with_enable, and custom.
The mux-lock DMUX scheme has the following restrictions:

       · Logic between the enabled Tx signal and the Rx signal has a MUX.

       · Rx output feeds back to the MUX input.

       · Logic between the Tx signal and the enabled Tx signal has a MUX and a second Tx register.

       · Tx register output feeds back to the MUX input.

       · First Tx, second Tx, and Rx drivers are registers.

       · A cdc dmux directive is used to specify the Tx lock signal (­tx_enable) and Rx lock signal
          (­rx_enable).

         Note:
         The physical design of the MUX logic (that controls the path from the Tx register to the Rx
         registers) must not allow glitches at the input to an Rx register when the Tx register changes
         value.

Use the cdc preference dmux directive to recognize CDC crossings as DMUX schemes where Tx or Rx
signals are memories (but not black box memories).

542            Questa® CDC User Guide
                                                                         Reference
                                                                  mux_lock_dmux

     1. Turn severity to evaluation:
            cdc report scheme mux_lock_dmux -severity evaluation

                                                                                        no_sync
no_sync

Single-bit signal does not have proper synchronizer. Default Severity: violation.
Crossing: 1-bit signal; Promotion: cdc_sample (default off); FX: yes (default on).

An unsynchronized CDC signal is typically a static violation, but if such a crossing terminates at a black
box module or RAM, the default severity is reported as caution (because synchronization might occur in
the black box). Similarly, a CDC signal synchronized using a 2DFF synchronizer that drives logic from the
wire connecting the two flip-flops is reported as a static violation by default.

Some signals from test or configuration logic might be constant or ad hoc synchronous with the receive
clock domain. Also, test or configuration logic driven by the wire connecting the two flip-flops of a 2DFF
synchronizer might also be constant or ad hoc synchronous with the receive clock domain. The severity of
these crossing schemes are typically set to caution.

Examples

     1. Turn severity to caution for the write_test signal in the module dut:

            cdc report scheme no_sync -severity caution

2. Example of a promoted transfer protocol checker for a no_sync synchronization (in
     cdc_protocol.rpt):

no_sync                                                                           

         module dut(input in, tx_clk, rx_clk, rst, output reg rx_sig);
         reg tx_sig;
         always @(posedge tx_clk, posedge rst)

                       if (rst)
                                      tx_sig<=1'b1;

                       else
                                      tx_sig<=in;

         always @(posedge rx_clk, posedge rst)
                       if (rst)
                                      rx_sig<=1'b1;
                       else
                                      rx_sig<=tx_sig;

         endmodule
         Violations

                                                                          pa_combo_logic
pa_combo_logic

UPF adds combinational logic to a crossing. Default Severity: violation.
Crossing: control signal and data bus; Promotion: none; FX: no.

Power-aware analysis adds logic defined in a UPF power specification to the HDL design logic. While
the CDC results for the HDL design might be OK, introducing logic implementing power intent can result
in additional clock domain crossing issues. The pa_combo_logic violation occurs when UPF logic adds
combinational logic to a previously-synchronized crossing resulting in a combo logic style violation.
For example, an isolation cell might introduce combinational logic (such as an isolation-enable MUX)
between the Tx output and the Rx synchronizer. Without the power-aware logic, the crossing is properly
synchronized. But, when the isolation cell is added, the MUX combinational logic breaks the crossing's
synchronization. You should do one of the following:

       · Add a Tx register just after the isolation cell (that is, combo logic).

       · If the contributing signals are stable, specify these with cdc signal -stable directives.

       · If the combinational logic output is constant during normal operation, glitches cannot be
          generated. Specify the signal that feeds the combinational logic as a constant value using the
          netlist constant directive.

       · If the violation is not an issue--a transfer protocol might ensure only one contributing signal
          changes value at a time--waive the violation.

Examples

     1. The following is an example to turn severity to caution:

            cdc report scheme pa_combo_logic -severity caution

     2. The following make target generates two reports:

            report :
              qverify -c -do " \
               cdc load db cdc.db; \
               cdc generate crossings crossings.rpt; \
               netlist generate pa pa_design_detail.rpt -design"

          The crossings report shows the details for pa_combo_logic violations.

      set_design_top top

        -primary_ground_net VSS

        mid1 Rx(clk2, tmp1, out1);
        mid1 Pwr_ctrl(clk2, in2, iso_en);

      module mid1(input clk, in1, output reg out1);

                        pa_fanin_different_clks

pa_fanin_different_clks

When UPF logic is added, the synchronizer has fanin from multiple clock domains. Default Severity:
violation.
Crossing: control signal; Promotion: none; FX: no.

Power-aware analysis adds logic defined in a UPF power specification to the HDL design logic. While the
CDC results for the HDL design might be OK, introducing logic implementing power intent can result in
additional clock domain crossing issues. The pa_fanin_different_clks violation occurs when UPF logic,
along with the RTL logic, results in a synchronizer's fanin logic coming from two clock domains. Without
the power-aware logic, the crossing might be properly synchronized. You should change the clock for the
isolation enable register to match the clock for the transmit signal.

               exit 0"

            (pa_fanin_different_clks)

  6. The following example continues Example 3: How to correct the problem illustrated in the
       example? As noted in the example, the logic has two issues: UPF adds combinational logic into
       the crossing and also makes the Rx fanin come from multiple domains. The solution is to correct
       both problems.

         Change the UPF to insert the isolation cell inside the tx_clk domain instead of at the crossing.
            Here is the excerpt from the incorrect UPF:

             create_power_domain PD_TX -elements {Tx1 Tx2}
             create_power_domain PD_RX -elements {Rx}
             ...
             set_isolation PD_TX_ISO_OUT -domain PD_RX -clamp_value Z \

                 -elements {Rx/in} -isolation_power_net VDD_HIGH \
                 -isolation_ground_net VSS

            Here is the corrected UPF:

             create_power_domain PD_TX -elements {Tx1}
             create_power_domain PD_RX -elements {Tx2
             Rx}
             ...
             set_isolation PD_TX_ISO_OUT -domain PD_RX -clamp_value Z \

                 -elements {Tx2/in} -isolation_power_net VDD_HIGH \
                 -isolation_ground_net VSS

Reference

       Put the Tx and power control clocks in the same clock domain. For example, add the
          following directive to the analysis setup:

           netlist clock pwr_iso_clk tx_clk -group TX;

     With these corrections, the crossing becomes a bus_two_dff evaluation.

                        pa_iso_en_no_sync

pa_iso_en_no_sync

UPF isolation cell enable signal does not have a proper synchronizer. Default Severity: violation.
Crossing: control signal; Promotion: none; FX: no.

Power-aware analysis adds logic defined in a UPF power specification to the HDL design logic. While the
CDC results for the HDL design might be OK, introducing logic implementing power intent can result in
additional clock domain crossing issues. The pa_iso_en_no_sync violation occurs when UPF logic adds
an isolation MUX whose enable signal comes unsynchronized from a different clock domain. Without the
power-aware logic, no crossing exists. But, when the isolation cell is added, the unsynchronized isolation
enable signal spawns a pa_iso_en_no_sync violation. You should try one of the following:

       · Add a Tx clock domain to the Rx clock domain synchronizer for the isolation enable signal in the
          source power domain logic.

       · If the isolation enable signal is stable, identify it with a cdc signal -stable directive.

               netlist generate pa pa_design_detail.rpt -design; \
               exit 0"

          The crossings report shows the details for pa_iso_en_no_sync violations.

                        pa_retention_restore

pa_retention_restore

UPF retention register restore port does not have a proper synchronizer. Default Severity: violation.
Crossing: control signal; Promotion: none; FX: no.

Power-aware analysis adds logic defined in a UPF power specification to the HDL design logic. While
the CDC results for the HDL design might be OK, introducing logic implementing power intent can result
in additional clock domain crossing issues. The pa_retention_restore violation occurs when UPF logic
adds a retention register, but the signal driving the register's restore port and the retention register are in
different clock domains. Without the power-aware logic, no crossing exists. But, when the UPF retention
logic is added, the unsynchronized retention restore signal spawns a pa_retention_restore violation. You
should try one of the following:

       · Check that the source of the restore signal has the correct clock.

       · Add a Tx clock domain to Rx clock domain synchronizer for the retention restore signal.

       · If the retention restore signal signal is stable, identify it with a cdc signal -stable directive.

            cdc report scheme pa_retention_restore -severity caution

        create_power_domain PD_intl -include_scope
        create_power_domain PD_gluelogic -elements { }

              -supply { perif_ssh } \

     The UPF logic inserts a retention register (INTERNAL_restore1) between two DFFs in the
     clk1 domain. However, the retention restore signal (restore1) comes directly from domain

CDC results for the HDL design might be OK, introducing logic implementing power intent can result in
additional clock domain crossing issues. The pa_retention_save violation occurs when UPF logic adds a
retention register, but the signal driving the register's save port and the retention register are in different
clock domains. Without the power-aware logic, no crossing exists. But, when the UPF retention logic is
added, the unsynchronized retention save signal spawns a pa_retention_save violation. You should try
one of the following:

       · Check that the source of the save signal has the correct clock.

       · Add a Tx clock domain to Rx clock domain synchronizer for the retention save signal.

       · If the retention save signal signal is stable, identify it with a cdc signal -stable directive.

Examples

     1. The following is an example to turn severity to caution:

            cdc report scheme pa_retention_save -severity caution

  2. The following example shows an instance of a pa_retention_save scheme. UPF for the design:

        set_design_top interleaver
        create_logic_port ret_en
        create_logic_port sw_en
        create_logic_port clamp_mem

        ## Top-level PD_intl which is always on
        create_power_domain PD_intl -include_scope
        create_power_domain PD_gluelogic -elements { }

        create_power_domain PD_intl -update \
              -supply { mem_ssh } \
              -supply { perif_ssh } \

Questa® CDC User Guide                                                                              563
Reference

partial_clock_gate_sync                                                                                     

          -supply { sram_ssh } \
          -supply { primary }
     set_retention glue_ret -domain PD_gluelogic -update \
          -save_signal { save posedge } \
          -restore_signal { restore negedge }

     The UPF logic inserts a retention register (INTERNAL_save1) between two DFFs in the
     clk1 domain. However, the retention save signal (save1) comes directly from domain clk2
     (unsynchronized). So the HDL logic has no clock domain crossing. However, the UPF logic adds
     a control signal with a missing (or invalid) synchronizer, which is identified as a pa_retention_save
     crossing (violation).

partial_clock_gate_sync

Structural clock gate synchronizer with failed functional check. Default Severity: caution.
Crossing: synchronized control signal and data bus at clock pin; Promotion: cdc_clockgate_sync
(default on); FX: none.

Structurally, partial_clock_gate_sync and clock_gate_sync are equivalent. In partial clock gate sync, we
have a signal from the TX clock domain, synchronized in the RX clock domain, and gated with the RX
clock. However, partial clock gate sync does not ensure that the synchronized signal can disable the
clock. If a crossing is a structural clock gate synchronizer but does not pass its functional check, it is
reported as an instance of a partial_clock_gate_sync scheme.

564                      Questa® CDC User Guide
                        Reference

                        partial_clock_gate_sync

Example

The partial_clock_gate_sync crossing matches the clock_gate_sync synchronizer structurally. However,
the synchronized enable signal (rx_sel) does not control the transfer of tx_data to dout. Regardless of
whether rx_sel is 1'b0 or 1'b1, the gating logic will always be rx_clk. Consequently, the select line does
not synchronize the transfer of Tx data to the Rx clock domain.

Sample DUT:

   module dut(input tx_clk, rx_clk, selin, din, rx_sig, rsta, rstb, output reg
     dout);

   reg tx_sel, sel, rx_sel, tx_data;
   always@(posedge tx_clk or negedge rsta) begin

      if(!rsta) tx_sel <= 1'b0;
      else tx_sel <= selin;
   end
   always@(posedge rx_clk or negedge rstb) begin
      if(!rstb) sel <= 1'b0;
      else sel <= tx_sel;
   end
   always@(posedge rx_clk or negedge rstb) begin
      if(!rstb) rx_sel <= 1'b0 ;
      else rx_sel <= sel;
   end
   // DATA
   always@(posedge tx_clk or negedge rsta) begin
      if(!rsta) tx_data <= 4'b0000;
      else tx_data <= din;
   end
   assign gated_clk = rx_sel ^ rx_clk;
   // OUT
   always@(posedge gated_clk or negedge rstb) begin
      if(!rstb) dout <= 4'b0000;
      else dout <= tx_data;
   end
   endmodule

Sample report:

   Cautions
   =================================================================
   Partial Clock gate synchronization (partial_clock_gate_sync)
   -----------------------------------------------------------------

                        partial_dmux

partial_dmux

Structural DMUX synchronization with functional check failure. Default Severity: caution.
Crossing: synchronized control signal and data bus; Promotion: cdc_dsel (default on); FX: yes (default
on).

Synchronization using a DMUX scheme is a standard method of synchronizing a data bus. The MUX
select signal can be synchronized by any of the following signal synchronizers: bus_dff_sync_gated_clk,
bus_four_latch, bus_two_dff, bus_two_dff_phase or two_dff_phase, dff_sync_gated_clk, four_latch,
two_dff, pulse_sync, custom_sync, dff_sync_with_enable, and custom_sync_with_crossing.

Structurally, dmux and partial_dmux schemes are similar. However, a dmux crossing additionally must
satisfy functional checks that ensure that the MUX select logic is determinant from the Tx domain. If a
crossing is a structural DMUX synchronizer but does not pass its functional check, it is reported as an
instance of a partial_dmux scheme. For a partial_dmux crossing, CDC analysis cannot determine that the
crossing's MUX selection prevents unstable data from passing through the MUX.

Use the cdc preference dmux directive to recognize CDC crossings as DMUX schemes where Tx or Rx
signals are memories (but not black box memories).

         Tip
         In most cases, you should change the partial_dmux scheme default severity to violation (using
         cdc reportscheme partial_dmuxseverity violation) to warn of the possibility of unstable data
         crossings. If appropriate, you can waive a partial_dmux crossing because it might be a valid
         DMUX-style synchronizer. For example, timing or other functional considerations for the MUX
         selection logic guarantees that the logic disables unstable data from passing through the MUX.

  CAUTION:
  A partial_dmux crossing is reported when the MUX select synchronizer is a
  custom_sync_mismatch crossing (i.e., instead of reporting the crossing as a no_sync crossing). If
  the mismatch is fixed, the crossing becomes a dmux crossing.

Examples

  1. Partial DMUX crossing matches a simple DMUX synchronizer structurally. However, the
       synchronized enable signal (rx_sel) does not solely control the transfer of tx_data to dout. If
       rx_sel is 1'b0 and rx_sig is 1'b1, then tx_data drives the dout register. Value of tx_data changes

Questa® CDC User Guide  567
Reference

partial_dmux                                           

     synchronously with tx_clk. But tx_data might change asynchronously to rx_clk, which might cause
     dout to be metastable.

     // SELECT
     always@(posedge tx_clk or negedge rsta) begin

        if(!rsta) tx_sel <= 1'b0;
        else tx_sel <= selin;
     end
     always@(posedge rx_clk or negedge rstb) begin
        if(!rstb) sel <= 1'b0;
        else sel <= tx_sel;
     end
     always@(posedge rx_clk or negedge rstb) begin
        if(!rstb) rx_sel <= 1'b0 ;
        else rx_sel <= sel;
     end
     always@(posedge rx_clk or negedge rstb) begin
        if(!rstb) rx_sig <= 1'b0 ;
        else rx_sig <= sig;
     end
     // DATA
     always@(posedge tx_clk or negedge rsta) begin
        if(!rsta) tx_data <= 4'b0000;
        else tx_data <= din;
     end
     assign w = rx_sel ^ rx_sig ? tx_data : dout;
     // OUT
     always@(posedge rx_clk or negedge rstb) begin
        if(!rstb) dout <= 4'b0000;
        else dout <= w;
     end

port_combo_logic  

port_combo_logic

Combinational logic before the primary output port that drives an external synchronizer. Default Severity:
violation.
Crossing: control signal or data bus; Promotion: none; FX: no.

If a primary output port of the current design drives external logic in a different clock domain, the design
environment must synchronize the signal from the output port to the driven logic. Typically this is done
by adding a synchronizer outside the design. However, CDC analysis cannot detect this external
synchronizer from information for the current design. To notify CDC analysis that a primary output port is
"externally synchronized" specify the external_sync option of the cdc port attribute command.
For example, the following command specifies that primary port a_to_clk2_sync drives a synchronizer
outside the current design:

   cdc port attribute a_to_clk2_sync -external_sync

If a primary port has the -external_sync attribute, CDC analysis checks to ensure the port is registered
--that is, whether or not the driver of the port (inside the current design) is a register (or latch). A port
that is not registered (that is, the port is driven by combinational logic) is reported as a port_combo_logic
violation.

Examples

     1. Turn severity to caution:

            cdc report scheme port_combo_logic ­severity caution

     2. The following example shows a primary output port with the external sync attribute. Here, the port
          is not registered, so the logic is reported as a port_combo_logic violation.

          Design  Questa® CDC User Guide
570
                        Reference

                        port_combo_logic

   module dut (
      input in1, in2, clk,
      output logic out);
      logic r1, r2;
      always @(posedge clk) begin
          r1 <= in1;
          r2 <= in2;
      end
      assign out = r1 & r2;

   endmodule

  Directives

   netlist clock clk
   cdc port attribute out -external_sync

pulse_single_edge

Pulse synchronization with a single edge. Default Severity: evaluation.
Crossing: single-bit control signal; Promotion: cdc_sync (default on); FX: yes (default on).

Pulse synchronization is a standard method of synchronizing a 1-bit signal. The Pulse Single Edge
scheme identifies pulse synchronizers that are either rising_edge or falling_edge. If both edges are used,
pulse_sync scheme is reported. This scheme is enabled with cdc scheme on pulse_single_edge directive.
If the directive is not specified, single-edge pulse syncs are reported as pulse_sync.

Examples

pulse_sync

Pulse synchronization. Default Severity: evaluation.
Crossing: 1-bit signal; Promotion: cdc_sync (default on); FX: yes (default on).

Pulse synchronization is a standard method of synchronizing a 1-bit signal. A variation of this scheme
happens if the pulse output is delayed. Specify the cdc preference -delayed_pulse directive to recognize
such schemes as pulse_sync schemes.

Another variation of pulse synchronization is a pulse_sync crossing where the initial pair of DFFs is
replaced by a custom synchronizer.

            cdc report scheme pulse_sync ­severity caution

                                                                                reconvergence

reconvergence

Reconvergence of synchronizers. Default Severity: caution.
Crossing: multiple control signals or data buses; Promotion: cdc_hamming_one (if enabled with cdc
preference protocol -promote_reconvergence); FX: no.

Fan-in of a flip-flop includes at least two separately synchronized CDC signals from a different clock
domain. By default, if any two reconverging CDC paths originate from the same bus, the scheme is
reported as a reconvergence_bus or reconvergence_mixed crossing. Reconvergence paths that do not
reconverge signals from the same bus are reported as reconvergence schemes.

The synchronizers can be any of the following: bus_dff_sync_gated_clk, bus_four_latch, bus_two_dff,
bus_two_dff_phase or two_dff_phase, dff_sync_gated_clk, four_latch, two_dff, pulse_sync, and custom.

Reconvergence analysis is OFF by default. Use cdc reconvergenceon to enable reconvergence analysis
for the design or for particular transmit/receive pairs of clock domains. When reconvergence analysis is
ON, the default depth of analysis is 0. Use cdc preference reconvergence-depth to increase the depth
of reconvergence analysis (and -divergence_depth to enable single-source reconvergence reporting in
addition to reconvergence reporting).

By default, the tool reports one reconvergence destination register for any supersets of the synchronizer
outputs converging at the same or different points. To view the report with all converging synchronizer
outputs separately, use cdc generate report ­verbose_reconvergence.

If it is not feasible to either design receiving logic that accounts for the potential cycle skew or encode
the signals, then you should group the signals and transfer them as a group using a synchronized
MUX enable (as used for multiple-bit data signals). To force CDC analysis to recognize reconvergence
schemes that start from a dmux, simple_dmux or multi_sync_mux_select scheme, specify cdc preference
reconvergence -dmux_as_recon_start.

         Tip
         To promote cdc_hamming_one checkers with the data_stability check turned on, specify cdc
         preference-sample_data_stability.

Examples

     1. The following example changes reconvergence depth to 4:
            cdc preference reconvergence -depth 4

  2. The following example disables reconvergence analysis to reduce run time.

Questa® CDC User Guide                                                                             579
Reference

reconvergence                                                                                     

     cdc reconvergence off

     3. The following example shows an instance of a reconvergence scheme that is reported when
          reconvergence depth is 0. The following code shows the reconvergence point and the two
          synchronizers on the reconverging paths.

           // Tx signals
           always @ (posedge tx_clk) begin

               tx1 <= in1;
               tx2 <= in2;
           end
           // two_dff synchronizer
           always @ (posedge rx_clk) begin: two_dff
               reg temp;
               temp <= tx1;
               two_dff_sync <= temp;
           end
           // two_dff synchronizer
           always @ (posedge rx_clk) begin: sync
               shift_reg_sync <= {shift_reg_sync[0], tx2};
           end
           // reconvergence point (depth 0)
           always @ (posedge rx_clk)
               dout <= two_dff_sync ^ shift_reg_sync[1];

   // Tx signals

reconvergence_bus

Reconvergence of bus bit synchronizers. Default Severity: violation.
Crossing: data buses; Promotion: cdc_hamming_one (if enabled with cdc preference
-promote_reconvergence); FX: no.

Fan-in of a register includes:

       · At least two separately synchronized CDC signals from bits of the same bus from a different clock
          domain.

       · No reconverging bits from a signal other than the reconverging bus.

The synchronizers can be any of the following: bus_dff_sync_gated_clk, bus_four_latch, bus_two_dff,
bus_two_dff_phase or two_dff_phase, dff_sync_gated_clk, four_latch, two_dff, pulse_sync and custom.

Reconvergence analysis is OFF by default. Use cdc reconvergence on to enable reconvergence analysis
for the design or for particular transmit/receive pairs of clock domains. When reconvergence analysis is
ON, the default depth of analysis is 0. Use cdc preference reconvergence -depth to increase the depth
of reconvergence analysis (and -divergence_depth to enable single-source reconvergence reporting in
addition to reconvergence reporting).

By default, the tool reports one reconvergence destination register for any supersets of the synchronizer
outputs converging at the same or different points. To view the report with all converging synchronizer
outputs separately, use cdc generate report ­verbose_reconvergence.

If it is not feasible to either design receiving logic that accounts for the potential cycle skew or encode
the signals, then you should group the signals and transfer them as a group using a synchronized
MUX enable (as used for multiple-bit data signals). To force CDC analysis to recognize reconvergence
schemes that start from a dmux, simple_dmux or multi_sync_mux_select scheme, specify cdc preference
reconvergence -dmux_as_recon_start.

         Tip
         : To promote cdc_hamming_one checkers with the data_stability check turned on, specify cdc
         preference-sample_data_stability.

Examples

     1. The following is an example that disables reconvergence analysis to reduce run time.
            cdc reconvergence off

                        reconvergence_bus

        module top (
            input tx_clk, rx_clk, input [1:0] din,
            output reg bus_bit_recon);
            reg [1:0] tx, x0, x1;
            always @(posedge tx_clk)
               tx <= din;
            always @(posedge rx_clk) begin
               // bus_two_dff
               x0 <= tx;
               x1 <= x0;
            end
            // Reconvergence
            always @ (negedge rx_clk)
               bus_bit_recon <= x1[0] & x1[1];

reconvergence_gray                                                                                     

reconvergence_gray

Reconvergence between gray-coded synchronized signals. Default Severity: evaluation.

Crossing: multiple control signals or data buses; Promotion: none (for default severity) and
cdc_hamming_one (for severity changed to caution and if enabled with cdc preference protocol
-promote_reconvergence); FX: no.

In this scheme, reconvergence happens between synchronized signals specified as gray coded using
the cdc signal -gray_coded command, which can be used to specify Tx, Rx, or the last register or latch in
the synchronizers. Usually, the last register in the synchronizer chains are reported as the start points in
reconvergence reports.

CDC analysis treats all signals specified in the same cdc signal -gray_coded directive as gray coded, and
flags reconvergence between these signals as reconvergence_gray. If the design contains numerous
reconvergence_gray schemes, you can eliminate these from CDC results using the cdc preference
reconvergence -no_graycode_recon option. Single-source reconvergence for gray-coded signals are
ignored because they do not constitute design issues.

By default, the tool reports one reconvergence destination register for any supersets of the synchronizer
outputs converging at the same or different points. To view the report with all converging synchronizer
outputs separately, use cdc generate report ­verbose_reconvergence.

         Note:
         You can also use the cdc signal -mutually_exclusive command interchangeably.

Examples

In this example, reconvergence is reported as reconvergence_gray with the default severity evaluation
using cdc signal tx_data -gray_coded (or cdc signal tx_data -mutually_exclusive):

module recon1

(

     input [1:0] i_data ,

     input  clk1 , clk2,

     output reg o_data

);

reg [1:0] tx_data ;
wire [1:0] rx_dataw ;

      begin

          tx_data <= i_data ;
      end

   .clk(clk2)) ;
two_dff #(1) sync1 (.din(tx_data[1]) , .dout(rx_dataw[1]) ,

reconvergence_mixed                                                                                

reconvergence_mixed

Reconvergence of mixed bus bit and other synchronizers. Default Severity: caution.
Crossing: multiple control signals or data buses; Promotion: cdc_hamming_one (if enabled with cdc
preference protocol -promote_reconvergence); FX: no.

Fan-in of a register includes:

       · At least two separately synchronized CDC signals from bits of the same bus from a different clock
          domain.

       · A reconverging bit from a signal other than the reconverging bus.

The synchronizers can be any of the following: bus_dff_sync_gated_clk, bus_four_latch, bus_two_dff,
bus_two_dff_phase or two_dff_phase, dff_sync_gated_clk, four_latch, two_dff, pulse_sync, and custom.

Reconvergence analysis is OFF by default. Use cdc reconvergence on to enable reconvergence analysis
for the design or for particular transmit/receive pairs of clock domains. When reconvergence analysis is
ON, the default depth of analysis is 0. Use cdc preference reconvergence -depth to increase the depth
of reconvergence analysis (and -divergence_depth to enable single-source reconvergence reporting in
addition to reconvergence reporting).

By default, the tool reports one reconvergence destination register for any supersets of the synchronizer
outputs converging at the same or different points. To view the report with all converging synchronizer
outputs separately, use cdc generate report ­verbose_reconvergence.

If it is not feasible to either design receiving logic that accounts for the potential cycle skew or encode
the signals, then you should group the signals and transfer them as a group using a synchronized
MUX enable (as used for multiple-bit data signals). To force CDC analysis to recognize reconvergence
schemes that start from a dmux, simple_dmux or multi_sync_mux_select scheme, specify cdc preference
reconvergence -dmux_as_recon_start.

         Tip
         To promote cdc_hamming_one checkers with the data_stability check turned on, specify cdc
         preference-sample_data_stability.

Examples

The following example shows an instance of a mixed reconvergence scheme.

586                                                                       Questa® CDC User Guide
                                                                    Reference
                                                     reconvergence_mixed
   module top (
      input tx_clk, rx_clk, din2, input [1:0] din1,
      output reg mixed_recon);
      reg [1:0] tx1, x0, x1;
      reg tx2, y0, y1;
      always @(posedge tx_clk) begin
          tx1 <= din1;
          tx2 <= din2;
      end
      always @(posedge rx_clk) begin
          // bus_two_dff
          x0 <= tx1 ;
          x1 <= x0 ;
          // two dff
          y0 <= tx2;
          y1 <= y0;
      end
      // Reconvergence
      always @ (negedge rx_clk)
          mixed_recon <= x1[0] & x1[1] & y1;

   endmodule

redundant                                                                   

redundant

Redundant synchronization. Default Severity: caution.
Crossing: multiple control signals or data buses; Promotion: none; FX: no.

Redundant synchronizers are multiple synchronizers in the same clock domain that synchronize the same
CDC signal. The values of the rx_sig1 and rx_sig2 signals might not match, because of metastability.
If these separately synchronized signals are in the fan-in of the same flip-flop, then a reconvergence
problem might exist. But, even if they are not, redundant synchronizers create extra logic that can be
eliminated by splitting the signals after they are synchronized.

Examples

     1. Redundant synchronizers: two dff synchronization:

     // two_dff synchronizer of tx_sig

     always @ (posedge rx_clk) begin: two_dff

           reg s0 , s1;

           s0 <= tx_sig; // 1st flop

           s1 <= s0;     // 2nd flop

     end

     // two_dff synchronizer of tx_sig

     always @ (posedge rx_clk) begin: sync

           reg [1:0] sh_reg;

           sh_reg <= {sh_reg[0], tx_sig};

     end

reg_enable_no_sync

                        series_redundant

series_redundant

Sync module/custom synchronizers connected in series or receiving input from same clock domain.
Default Severity: caution.

Crossing: multiple control signals or data buses; Promotion: none; FX: no.

Series redundant synchronizers are sync module/custom synchronizers that either connect in series to
synchronize with the same clock domain or are single synchronizers receiving input from the same clock
domain they synchronize to. To determine if two sync module/custom synchronizers in series are in the
same domain, match the clock domain of the Tx synchronizer output with the clock domain of the Rx
synchronizer input. Additionally, if a single sync module or custom synchronizer has an input driven by
a signal from the same clock domain it synchronizes to, it is also considered redundant, and the Questa
CDC tool will report it as series_redundant.

By default, detection of series_redundant scheme is off. Use cdc scheme on series_redundant to turn
on the detection. Series-redundant synchronizers do not indicate CDC problems, but they do indicate a
waste of logic and power consumption.

Examples

  1. The top module demonstrates custom synchronizers connected in series to ensure reliable data
       transfer between different clock domains.

       Sample Design

        module top(input d1, d2, clk1, clk2, rst, output q);
            reg tx;
            wire o1;
            always@(posedge clk1 or negedge rst)
               if(!rst)
                   tx<=1'b0;
               else
                   tx<=d1;

            custom_sync s1(tx, clk2, rst, o1);
            custom_sync s2(o1, clk2, rst, q);
        endmodule

        module sync(input d, clk, rst, output reg q);
            reg rx;
            always@(posedge clk or negedge rst)
               if(!rst) begin
                   rx<=1'b0;
                   q<=1'b0;
               end

Questa® CDC User Guide                                                                           597

            else begin
               rx<=d;
               q<=rx;

                        simple_dmux

simple_dmux

Simple MUX enable. Default Severity: caution.
Crossing: synchronized control signal and muxed data bus; Promotion: cdc_dsel (default on); FX: yes
(default on).

The simple DMUX scheme is a restricted version of the general DMUX scheme. For the general scheme,
the fanin logic of the Rx signal can contain any logic and the synchronized control signal can use any
logic to turn off he Tx signal (not just a MUX). The control signal can be synchronized by any of the
following signal synchronizers: two_dff_phase, dff_sync_gated_clk, four_latch, two_dff, pulse_sync and
custom.
The simple DMUX scheme has the following restrictions:

       · Logic between the Tx and Rx signals has a MUX.

       · Rx output feeds back to the MUX input.

       · Tx signal drives the D-input of the Rx register.

       · Tx and Rx drivers are registers.

       · No combo logic is between the Tx and Rx registers.

       · No combo logic is between select output from the synchronizer and the MUX.

         Note:
         The physical design of the MUX logic (that controls the path from the Tx register to the Rx
         registers) must not allow glitches at the input to an Rx register when the Tx register changes
         value.

Use the cdc preference dmux directive to recognize CDC crossings as DMUX schemes where Tx or Rx
signals are memories (but not black box memories).

Questa® CDC User Guide  605
Reference

single_source_reconvergence                                                                        

single_source_reconvergence

Single-source reconvergence of synchronizers. Default Severity: violation.
Crossing: multiple control signals or data buses; Promotion: cdc_hamming_one (if enabled with cdc
preference protocol -promote_reconvergence); FX: no.

Reconvergence occurs when the fan-in of a flip-flop includes two separately synchronized CDC signals
from a different clock domain. Single-source reconvergence is the special case where reconverging
signals in the receive domain originate from the same signal in the transmit domain. Reconvergent
signals might result in synchronization problems, but large designs can have large numbers of
reconvergence paths. Single-source reconvergence paths are more likely to cause design problems than
reconvergence paths from unrelated sources, so they can be given a higher priority when resolving issues
of reconvergence.

By default, the tool reports one reconvergence destination register for any supersets of the synchronizer
outputs converging at the same or different points. To view the report with all converging synchronizer
outputs separately, use cdc generate report ­verbose_reconvergence.

Static CDC analysis reports single-source reconvergence paths as both reconvergence violations and
SSR violations. To determine how extensive static CDC analysis of reconvergence paths should be,
adjust the following parameters using the cdc preference reconvergence directive:

       · depth

          Maximum number of sequential levels in the receive domain from the synchronizers to the
          reconverging paths. The depth is used to limit analysis of reconverging paths (both single-source
          and separate-source).

       · divergence_depth

          Maximum number of sequential levels in the transmit domain from the flip-flops driving the
          synchronizers backwards to the single source. The depth is used to limit the analysis of single-
          source reconverging paths. The transmit register is at depth 0, the registers driving the transmit
          register are at depth 1, and so on. Default value: 0.

By default, when reconvergence is enabled with cdc reconvergence on, CDC analysis checks single-
source reconvergence with divergence_depth set to 0. Zero divergence depth is commonly associated
with reconvergence of redundant synchronizers. In this case, the transmit signal is redundantly
synchronized, and the duplicate synchronized signals combine in an out-of-sync manner. To enable
reconvergence checks without single-source reconvergence, specify a negative divergence depth to
override the default value 0.

608                          Questa® CDC User Guide
                                                                                       Reference

single_source_reconvergence                                                                                

     5. The following example shows an instance of a single-source reconvergence scheme that is
          reported when divergence depth is 0. SSR reporting is off by default, so turn on SSR reporting:

           cdc preference reconvergence -divergence_depth 0

          The following code shows the divergence and reconvergence points and the two synchronizers
          on the reconverging paths.

           // divergence point
           always @ (posedge tx_clk)

               ctrl <= ci0 | ci1 ;
           // two_dff synchronizer
           always @ (posedge rx_clk) begin: two_dff

               reg temp;
               temp <= ctrl;
               two_dff_sync <= temp;
           end
           // two_dff synchronizer
           always @ (posedge rx_clk) begin: sync
               shift_reg_sync <= {shift_reg_sync[0], ctrl};
           end
           // reconvergence point
           always @ (posedge rx_clk)
               dout <= two_dff_sync ^ shift_reg_sync[1];

  // reconvergence point

  always @ ( posedge rx_clk )

  dout <= two_dff_sync - shift_reg_sync[7:4];

                                                                                            sync_enable

sync_enable

Enable signal driving the combinational logic controls data. Default Severity: evaluation.
Crossing: synchronized data bus; Promotion: cdc_dsel (default on); FX: yes (default off).

A crossing with sync_enable scheme must satisfy functional checks ensure that the enable signal controls
the transmitting data. Although it is highly recommended that the crossing must pass the functional
checks, you can use the -disable_control_check argument with the cdc preference syncenable directive to
skip the functional checks.

By default, the scheme does not verify if the enable signal is driven by a synchronizer. Use the
-rx_enable_sync argument with the cdc preference syncenable directive to enable checking of a
synchronizer before the enable signal.

         Note:
         The physical design of the MUX logic (that controls the path from the Tx register to the Rx
         registers) must not allow glitches at the input to an Rx register when the Tx register changes
         value.

Examples

     1. The following example shows a crossing with sync_enable scheme where the MUX is driven by
          the rx_sel signal which is defined as the rx_enable signal in the directives.

          Design

            module dut(input tx_clk, rx_clk, data, sel, output reg q);
              reg tx_data, tx_sel;
              reg s1, rx_sel;
              reg rx_data;
              reg r1;
              always@(posedge tx_clk) tx_data <= data;
              always@(posedge rx_clk) rx_sel <= sel;
              mux m1(.tx_data(tx_data), .rx_clk(rx_clk),
                 .rx_sel(rx_sel), .rx_data(rx_data));
              always @(posedge rx_clk) q <= rx_data;
              always @(posedge rx_clk) begin: MUX

        else r1 <= rx_data;

sync_module

Synchronization of a 1-bit signal. Default Severity: evaluation.

Crossing: 1-bit signal; Promotion: cdc_sync (default on); FX: yes (default off).

Reports the Valid DFF structures, for single-bit crossings which satisfy the cdc syncmodule specification
constraint in case the syncmodule flow is on.

If sync_module specification fails, it gets reported as no_sync.
Directives

       · Use the directive to switch on all DFF and related sync variations like pulse sync, async_reset
          sync and so on, if the syncmodule specification fails.

            cdc preference report_dff_type_on_syncmodule_fail

          The report_dff_type_on_syncmodule_fail option is applicable only when the sync_module flow is
          enabled.

       · For a valid DFF path for which the sync_module flow is enabled, but the syncmodule specification
          fails on the path, by default the path is not reported as DFF. A check is made if any other valid
          synchronizer like DMux is present, and report no_sync if no synchronizers, other than DFF, are
          found.

Examples

two_dff

Single-bit signal synchronized by DFF synchronizer. Default Severity: evaluation.
Crossing: 1-bit signal; Promotion: cdc_sync (default on); FX: yes (default off).

Synchronization using two flip-flops is a standard method of synchronizing a 1-bit signal.

Examples

     1. The following is an example to turn severity to caution:
            cdc report scheme two_dff ­severity caution

2. The following is an example to turn off promotion:
      cdc promote scheme two_dff ­promotion off

3. Example of a promoted transfer protocol checker for the two_dff synchronization scheme (in
     cdc_protocol.rpt):

Type/Scheme : cdc_sync top.two_dff_28808

Check data stable         : On <Default On>

TX SIGNAL                 : GEN.dsc_inst0.cont_reg_d_0

TX CLOCK                  : tx_clk

TX_MIN                    :2

4. A single-bit signal synchronized by two cascaded flip-flops:

module dut(input in, tx_clk, rx_clk, output reg s1);

reg tx_sig, s0;

always @(posedge tx_clk)

tx_sig<=in;

always @(posedge rx_clk) begin

s0<=tx_sig; // 1st DFF

s1<=s0;                 // 2nd DFF

end

endmodule

If you use a DFF synchronization scheme that has more than two flip-flops, then you can get CDC
analysis to recognize the scheme by specifying a cdc synchronizer directive. For example, the following
CDC directive identifies 4 DFF synchronizers as valid "two_dff" schemes for CDC paths from the tx_clk
domain to the rx_clk domain:

   cdc synchronizer dff -level 4 -tx_clock tx_clk -rx_clock rx_clk

two_dff_phase

Single-bit signal synchronized by the DFF of opposite clock polarity. Default Severity: caution.
Crossing: 1-bit signal; Promotion: cdc_sync (default on); FX: yes (default off).

Synchronization using two opposite polarity flip-flops has a reduced time for rx_sig to settle. When using
this synchronization scheme, be sure the MTBF is acceptable.

Examples

            cdc report scheme two_dff_phase -severity caution

     2. A 2-DFF phase synchronizer has one FF clocked by a clock with the opposite polarity of the Rx
          clock:

            always @(negedge rx_clk)
               sync1 <= tx_sig; // 1st FF

            always @(posedge rx_clk)
               sync2 <= sync1; // 2nd FF

                                                              CDC Protocol Checkers

CDC Protocol Checkers

A protocol checker is associated with a CDC synchronizer. Each protocol checker contains a set of
checks that checks the CDC synchronizer protocol. Checks are written in the standard SystemVerilog
Assertion (SVA) language.

Table 34 lists the CDC protocol checker types.

                        Table 34. CDC Protocol Checker Types

Checker Type            Description
cdc_dsel
cdc_fifo                Verifies that a multi-bit Tx signal synchronized by a DMUX-style
cdc_glitch              synchronizer remains stable long enough for the Rx logic to
cdc_hamming_one         properly sample the signal's value.
cdc_handshake           Verifies that a FIFO-style crossing synchronizes a multi-bit Tx
cdc_sample              signal so that Rx logic correctly samples the Tx values.
                        Verifies that a single-bit input to Rx logic changes value at most
cdc_sync                once each Rx clock cycle.
cdc_clockoff            Verifies that when a multibit Tx signal changes value, it only
cdc_clockgate_sync      changes value by hamming distance 1 and the value remains
                        stable for a specified number of Tx clock cycles.
                        Verifies that a handshake-style crossing synchronizes a multi-bit
                        Tx signal so that Rx logic correctly samples the Tx values.
                        Verifies that when a multi-bit Tx signal is sampled in the Rx
                        domain, its Tx value remains stable in the setup period before
                        the value is sampled and the hold period after the value is
                        sampled, or both.
                        Verifies that a single-bit signal crossing from a faster to a slower
                        clock domain is stable long enough for the Rx logic to correctly
                        sample the signal's value.
                        Ensures that a signal crossing through cdc is safe from
                        metastability as the receiver clock is turned off when the its
                        asychronous reset de-asserts.
                        Ensures that signals passing through a clock-gated synchronizer
                        are reliably sampled by the receiver. It verifies that the receiver
                        input (rx_data) remains stable for one clock cycle when the
                        receiver clock (rx_clock) is active, thereby ensuring data
                        integrity under clock gating conditions.

Questa® CDC User Guide                                                                              625

                                                    FX Checkers

FX Checkers

FX Checkers are specialized tools associated with CDC synchronizers. Each FX Checker contains a set
of checks that model and analyze the effects of metastability on clock domain crossings. These checks
help ensure the reliability and accuracy of CDC synchronizers by propagating metastability effects to the
output values of receive registers.

Table 35 lists the FX checker types.

                        Table 35. FX Checker Types

Checker Type            Description
cdc_fx
                        Models random metastability injected on a clock domain
cdc_mfx                 crossing from a transmit register to a receive register.
                        Propagates the metastability effects to output values for the
cdc_pfx                 receive register.
cdc_rfx                 Models random metastability injected on multiple clock domain
                        crossings from multiple transmit registers in different frequencies
                        to a single receive register. Propagates the metastability effects
                        to output values for the receive register.
                        Models random metastability injected on a clock domain
                        crossing from a transmit port to a receive register. Propagates
                        the metastability effects to output values for the receive register.
                        Models random metastability injected on a clock domain
                        crossing from a transmit register to a receive register due to
                        reset deassertion. Propagates the metastability effects to output
                        values for the receive register.

Checks

       · cdc_fx (default On)

          assert_cdc_fx

          Tx register output is not stable in the receiving register's metastability window.

          Typically, the data output of a clock doman crossing's transmit register can change value in the
          receive register's metastability window. This change can cause metastability of the receiving
          register's output, but the circuit is hopefully tolerant of this effect.

          However, an ad hoc synchronizer might presume the transmit logic prevents the transmitting
          register from changing value in the receiving register's metastability window. Therefore, the ad
          hoc synchronizer logic assumes the receiving register cannot become metastable. In this case,
          the cdc_fx check can be used to verify the transmit value is held stable whenever the transmit/
          receive clocks are aligned. Here, the cdc_fx check is a transmit protocol check for the ad hoc
          synchronizer.

                  Note:
                  By default, the cdc_fx check is off for the crossings that are reported as evaluation.

     Eval: @(posedge tx_clk) !rx_reset && rx_load_enable && rx_data_tx_d != rx_data
     Firing message: Data changed in metastability window setup = setup_percent, hold =
     hold_percent.

                        cdc_fx

Description

Models the effects of injecting random metastability at the input port of the Rx register in a clock domain
crossing. Metastability is injected in random cycles for which the Tx and Rx clocks are "aligned." That
is, the Tx clock's active edge activates within the metastability window of the Rx active clock edge. The
metastability window is defined in percentage of the Rx clock period: the setup region before the Rx clock
edge and the hold region after the Rx clock edge.

By default, the setup region is 25% of the Rx clock period and the hold region is 10% of the Rx clock
period. Specification for the metastability window is modified with the cdcfx fx window directive.

         Tip
         Directive cdcfx fx window sets the maximum size of the metastability window. The two end points
         of the window are not included in the window. So, if an active Tx clock edge falls on the boundary,
         it is considered outside the window. In addition, two metastability windows around adjacent Rx
         clock edges cannot overlap. So, the fx_clocks_aligned monitor adjusts window strobes to prevent
         this. In particular, the sizes of the metastability windows might dynamically change during the
         entire simulation.

To model the effects of metastability at the input to the Rx register, each metastable bit is randomly flipped
and the result is output at the checker's rx_reg_metastable port. The simulation design with CDC-FX
metastability injection modeling is created by connecting CDC-FX checkers. Checkers and clocks-aligned
monitors are instantiated by binding their inputs to their associated crossing signals. Output from the
modeled rx_reg_metastable ports are forced on the wires driven by the original rx_reg outputs of the
crossings' receive registers (Figure 121).

                                         Figure 121. CDC-FX Checker Connection

clks_aligned[65:0]

Clocks aligned monitor sends Tx/Rx clock alignment information to its cdc_fx checker via the clks_aligned
bus. The monitor considers Tx/Rx clocks are aligned for an Rx clock cycle if an active Tx clock edge
activates within the metastability window around the Rx clock edge. Tx clock edges at the window
boundaries are considered to be outside the window. End points of each window cannot be larger than
those specified by -start and -stop arguments to the clock's cdcfx fx window directive (default:25% start;
10% stop). Start and stops points might be smaller than specified, to eliminate window overlaps.

Value of clks_aligned is non-zero if, and only if, the Tx/Rx clocks are aligned in the matching Rx clock
cycle. Value changes one time unit after the active Rx clock edge and returns to 0 at the next active Rx
clock edge. The 1 unit delay is needed to avoid race conditions. Bits of the clks_aligned bus have these
values (Figure 122):

       · clks_aligned[0]

          Setup region strobe. Tx clock edge is in the Rx setup region (i.e., it is before the Rx clock edge).

Questa® CDC User Guide  661
Reference

cdc_fx                                                                                                      

     · clks_aligned[1]
        Hold region strobe. Tx clock edge is in the Rx hold region (i.e., it is at, or after, the Rx clock
        edge).

     · clks_aligned[33:2]
        Number of time units from the Rx clock edge to the start point of the window.

     · clks_aligned[65:34]
        Number of time units from the Rx clock edge to the stop point of the window

                                                Figure 122. clks_aligned[1:0]

cdc_pfx                                                                                            

Description

Models the effects of injecting random metastability at the input port of the Rx register typically driven by
multiple clock domain crossings. Metastability is injected in random cycles for which one of the Tx clocks
and the Rx clock are "aligned." That is, a Tx clock's active edge activates within the MFX metastability
window of the Rx active clock edge. The MFX metastability window is defined in percentage of the Rx
clock period and applies only to the setup region before the Rx clock edge.

By default, the setup region is 25% of the Rx clock period. Specification for the MFX metastability window
is modified with the cdcfx mfx window directive.

         Tip
         Directive cdcfx mfx window sets the maximum size of the metastability window. The start points of
         the window is not included in the window. So, if an active Tx clock edge falls on the start point, it
         is considered outside the window.

By default, cdc_fx checkers are promoted for Rx registers driven from a single clock domain and cdc_mfx
checkers are promoted for Rx checkers driven from multiple clock domains. You can use cdc_mfx
metastability injection modeling for all promoted checkers by specifying: cdcfx on -all_mfx.

To model the effects of metastability at the bits input to the Rx register, each metastable bit is randomly
flipped and the result is output at the checker's rx_reg_metastable port. The simulation design with CDC-
FX metastability injection modeling is created by connecting CDC-FX checkers. Checkers and clocks-
aligned monitors are instantiated by binding their inputs to their associated crossing signals. Output from
the modeled rx_reg_metastable ports are forced on the wires driven by the original rx_reg outputs of the
crossings' receive registers. Figure 123 shows a cdc_mfx checker promoted for an rx_data register with
bits from two multi-bit clock domain crossings.

                                        Figure 123. CDC-MFX Checker Connection

cdc_pfx

Models random metastability injected on a clock domain crossing from a transmit port to a receive
register. Propagates the metastability effects to output values for the receive register.

Checks

       · cdc_pfx (default On)

          assert_cdc_pfx

          Tx port is not stable in the receiving register's metastability window. Usually, the value of a clock
          domain crossing's transmit port can alter within the receive register's metastability window. This
          alteration may induce metastability in the output of the receiving register, but the circuit ideally
          tolerates this effect. The cdc_pfx check can be used to verify that the transmit value remains
          stable whenever the transmit clock is in the setup metastability window of the receive clock.

                  Note:
                  cdc_pfx only checks the stability of transmit port in the setup metastability window of the
                  Rx (receive) register.

     Firing message: Data changed in metastability window.

             cp_clocks_aligned_cycles

             cp_clocks_aligned_cycles
                Number of cycles in which the checker injects metastability and the Tx clock edge activates
                before the Rx clock edge.

             cp_delayed_transitions
                Number of cycles in which the effect of metastability injection is to delay the data driving the
                rx_reg_metastable output by one cycle.

Description

Models the effects of injecting random metastability at the input port of the Rx register typically driven by
clock domain crossing with transmit signal as port. Metastability is injected in random cycles for which
the Tx and Rx clocks are "aligned." That is, the Tx clock's active edge activates within the metastability
window of the Rx active clock edge. The metastability window is defined in percentage of the Rx clock
period: the setup region before the Rx clock edge and the hold region after the Rx clock edge.

         Note:
         PFX only works in the setup metastability window.

By default, the setup region is 25% of the Rx clock period. Specification for the metastability window is
modified with the cdcfx fx window directive.

To model the effects of metastability at the bits input to the Rx register, each metastable bit is randomly
flipped and the result is output at the checker's rx_reg_metastable port. The simulation design with
cdc_pfx metastability injection modeling is created by connecting cdc_pfx checkers. Checkers and clocks-
aligned monitors are instantiated by binding their inputs to their associated crossing signals. Output from
the modeled rx_reg_metastable ports are forced on the wires driven by the original rx_reg outputs of the
crossings' receive registers. Figure 124 shows a cdc_pfx checker promoted for an rx_data register with
bits from two multi-bit clock domain crossings. The Tx clock will be associated with the netlist clock.

cdc_rfx

Models random metastability injected on a clock domain crossing from a transmit register to a receive
register due to reset deassertion. Propagates the metastability effects to output values for the receive
register.

By default, cdc_rfx is off. To enable it, use cdc preference -promote_async_reset.

 rx_load_enable,

Checks

       · cdc_rfx (default On)

          assert_cdc_rfx

          Tx register output is not stable and may deassert receiving register in the in the receiving
          register's metastability window.

          Typically, the data output of a clock doman crossing's transmit register can change value and can
          deassert receive register in the receive register's metastability window. This change can cause
          metastability of the receiving register's output, but the circuit is hopefully tolerant of this effect.

Questa® CDC User Guide                                                              671
Reference

cdc_rfx                                                                                                    

         However, an ad hoc synchronizer might presume the transmit logic prevents the transmitting
         register from changing value in the receiving register's metastability window. Therefore, the ad
         hoc synchronizer logic assumes the receiving register cannot become metastable. In this case,
         the cdc_rfx check can be used to verify that the receiver input is not changing when transmit
         value (receiver areset) deasserts within receive clock metastability window. Here, the cdc_rfx
         check is a transmit protocol check for the ad hoc synchronizer.

         Eval: @(negedge rx_areset) !rx_reset && rx_load_enable && rx_adata != rx_data

         Firing message: Data changed as asynchronous reset de-asserted in the metastability window
         setup = setup_percent, hold = hold_percent.

Description

Models the effects of injecting random metastability at the input port of the Rx register in a clock domain
crossing. Metastability is injected in all cycles for which the Rx areset deassertion and Rx clocks are
"aligned." That is, the Rx asynchronous reset desserts within the metastability window of the Rx active
clock edge. The metastability window is defined in percentage of the Rx clock period: the setup region
before the Rx clock edge and the hold region after the Rx clock edge.

By default, the setup region is 25% of the Rx clock period and the hold region is 10% of the Rx clock
period. Specification for the metastability window is modified with the cdcfx fx window directive.

  Tip
  Directive cdcfx fx window sets the maximum size of the metastability window. The two end points
  of the window are not included in the window. So, if rx areset deasserts on the boundary, it is
  considered outside the window. In addition, two metastability windows around adjacent Rx clock
  edges cannot overlap. So, the fx_reset_clks_aligned monitor adjusts window strobes to prevent
  this. In particular, the sizes of the metastability windows might dynamically change during the
  entire simulation.

To model the effects of metastability at the input to the Rx register, each metastable bit is randomly flipped
and the result is output at the checker's rx_reg_metastable port. The simulation design with CDC-RFX
metastability injection modeling is created by connecting CDC-RFX checkers. Checkers and areset clock-

Questa® CDC User Guide                                                                          673
Reference

cdc_rfx                                                                                                      

aligned monitors are instantiated by binding their inputs to their associated crossing signals. Output from
the modeled rx_reg_metastable ports are forced on the wires driven by the original rx_reg outputs of the
crossings' receive registers (Figure 125).

     Note:
     Since reset signals do not toggle frequently during simulation, it is beneficial to force FX injection
     whenever rx_clock and rx_areset are aligned and sampling is enabled.

           Figure 125. CDC-RFX Checker Connection

clk_arst_aligned[65:0]

Clock areset aligned monitor sends Rx clock/areset alignment information to its cdc_rfx checker via the
clk_arst_aligned bus. The monitor considers Rx clock/areset are aligned for an Rx clock cycle if an active
Tx a rx areset deasserts within the metastability window around the Rx clock edge. Rx areset deassertion
edge at the window boundaries are considered to be outside the window. End points of each window
cannot be larger than those specified by -start and -stop arguments to the clock's cdc fx window directive
(default:25% start; 10% stop). Start and stops points might be smaller than specified, to eliminate window
overlaps.

Value of clk_arst_aligned is non-zero if, and only if, the Rx clock and areset deassertion are aligned in
the matching Rx clock cycle. Value changes one time unit after the active Rx clock edge and returns
to 0 at the next active Rx clock edge. The 1 unit delay is needed to avoid race conditions. Bits of the
clk_arst_aligned bus have these values (Figure 126):

       · clk_arst_aligned[0]

          Setup region strobe. Rx areset deassertion is in the Rx setup region (that is, it is before the Rx
          clock edge).

       · clk_arst_aligned[1]

          Hold region strobe. Rx asreset deassertion is in the Rx hold region (that is, it is at, or after, the Rx
          clock edge).

674                                                Questa® CDC User Guide
                                                                                         Reference
                                                                                             cdc_rfx
       · clk_arst_aligned[33:2]
          Number of time units from the Rx clock edge to the start point of the window.

       · clk_arst_aligned[65:34]
          Number of time units from the Rx clock edge to the stop point of the window
